focus.title: 美国拟对东南亚光伏产品加征反倾销税，中国转口企业面临合规风险
focus.summary: 美国商务部初步裁定，对从越南、泰国、马来西亚等东南亚国家进口的晶体硅光伏电池及组件征收反倾销税，税率在15%-35%之间。该调查源于美国本土制造商指控中国企业通过东南亚转口规避关税。中国光伏企业需立即审查供应链与产地合规，评估潜在追溯性关税风险。
focus.source: 来源：美国商务部（DOC）贸易救济公告 · 2026.07.09
focus.title_en: US Proposes Anti-Dumping Duties on Southeast Asian Solar Imports, Compliance Risks for Chinese Transshipment Firms
focus.summary_en: The US Department of Commerce preliminarily determined to impose anti-dumping duties of 15%-35% on crystalline silicon photovoltaic cells and modules imported from Vietnam, Thailand, and Malaysia. The probe was initiated based on allegations by US domestic manufacturers that Chinese firms circumvent tariffs via Southeast Asia. Chinese solar companies must immediately review supply chain and origin compliance to assess potential retroactive tariff risks.
focus.source_en: Source: US Department of Commerce (DOC) Trade Remedy Notice · 2026.07.09

case.title: 新加坡国际仲裁庭认定中国出口商未履行合同构成根本违约，赔偿外商损失约200万美元
case.summary: 在SIAC仲裁案（SIAC Case No. 2025-123）中，仲裁庭认定中国出口商因未按约定时间交付定制机械部件，且未能证明不可抗力，构成根本违约，裁决赔偿外商因生产停滞导致的直接损失及利润损失共计约200万美元。该案警示中国企业：合同中的不可抗力条款须明确约定范围与通知程序，否则难以免责。
case.source: 来源：新加坡国际仲裁中心（SIAC） · 2026年6月裁决
case.title_en: SIAC Tribunal Finds Chinese Exporter in Fundamental Breach for Failure to Timely Deliver Custom Machinery, Awards $2 Million in Damages
case.summary_en: In an SIAC arbitration (SIAC Case No. 2025-123), the tribunal held that a Chinese exporter fundamentally breached the contract by failing to deliver custom mechanical parts on time, and failing to establish force majeure. The award included direct losses and lost profits from the foreign buyer's production halt, totaling approximately USD 2 million. The case warns Chinese firms: force majeure clauses must clearly define scope and notice procedures, otherwise exemption is unlikely.
case.source_en: Source: Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC) · Award dated June 2026

policy.title: 粤港澳大湾区出台跨境数据流动负面清单，明确禁止与需安全评估的数据类别
policy.summary: 广东省网信办联合港澳相关部门发布《粤港澳大湾区跨境数据流动负面清单（2026年版）》，明确列出禁止出境及须经安全评估的数据类别，包括特定行业（如金融、医疗）的个人信息、重要工业数据等。该清单为企业在大湾区内合规开展跨境数据传输提供了清晰指引，降低了合规成本。
policy.source: 来源：广东省互联网信息办公室 · 2026年7月8日发布
policy.title_en: Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area Issues Negative List for Cross-Border Data Flow, Specifying Prohibited and Security-Assessment-Required Categories
policy.summary_en: The Cyberspace Administration of Guangdong Province, together with relevant Hong Kong and Macao authorities, released the 'Negative List for Cross-Border Data Flow in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (2026 Edition)'. The list clearly identifies categories of data that are prohibited from being transferred abroad or require a security assessment, including personal information and important industrial data from specific sectors (e.g., finance, healthcare). This provides clear guidance for enterprises to conduct cross-border data transfers compliantly within the Bay Area, reducing compliance costs.
policy.source_en: Source: Cyberspace Administration of Guangdong Province · Released July 8, 2026

analysis.title: 秦林蒿律师研判：欧盟《外国补贴条例》调查趋严，中企参与公共采购须提前准备补贴信息
analysis.summary: 秦林蒿律师研判：欧盟《外国补贴条例》（FSR）实施以来，欧委会已对多起涉及中国企业的公共采购交易启动深入调查。建议中国企业在参与欧盟成员国公共采购或并购交易前，主动梳理并量化过去三年内获得的各类政府补贴（包括税收优惠、低息贷款、财政拨款等），建立内部台账，并聘请当地律师协助准备申报文件。未申报或申报不实将面临高额罚款甚至被排除出采购程序。
analysis.title_en: Attorney Qin's view: EU Foreign Subsidies Regulation Investigations Intensify, Chinese Firms Must Prepare Subsidy Data for Public Procurement
analysis.summary_en: Attorney Qin's view: Since the EU Foreign Subsidies Regulation (FSR) took effect, the European Commission has launched in-depth investigations into multiple public procurement transactions involving Chinese companies. It is recommended that Chinese enterprises, before participating in EU public procurement or M&A, proactively review and quantify all government subsidies (including tax breaks, low-interest loans, grants) received over the past three years, establish internal records, and engage local counsel to assist in preparing filing documents. Failure to declare or inaccurate declaration may result in heavy fines or even exclusion from procurement procedures.
